model: Regulated utility free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; rate-base equity compounding, net debt zero)

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares for Q3 2026 (10-Q, 278.9m; includes 1.0m treasury-stock dilution from outstanding forward sale agreements). Held FLAT: all equity the plan requires -- the 6.4m forward shares settling in Q4 2026 and the ~$5bn 2027-2031 programme -- is charged as a cash call to today's holders inside the flows (the 'capex' line), so compounding the count as well would charge the dilution twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Set to zero BY DESIGN: the flow discounted is free cash flow to EQUITY (net income less equity retained/raised to fund rate-base growth), which is already after $776m (FY2025) / $629m (9M-2026) of interest charges. Deducting the $22.5bn of debt again would double-count it. Actual balance-sheet debt is recorded in total_debt / cash / net_debt_actual for the reader.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 free cash flow to equity = dividends paid 768 - common stock issued 574 = 194 (equivalently NI 1,456 less the 1,262 increase in shareholders' equity ex-NCI, 12,139 -> 13,401). The firm-level owner FCF (OCF 3,353 - capex 4,128 - SBC 28) is -803 and is structurally negative through at least 2031 -- see inputs.notes for why it is not the valuation flow.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation costs' 28 (FY2024 28, FY2023 26); equity-award taxes 13 are inside the net-share settlement line and are not added on top. SBC is already expensed in net income, so the FCFE build carries sbc_pct_path at 0 rather than deducting it a second time.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:03Z regular close (Friday); valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print involved
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is to equity. USD build: 10-year UST 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-06), 30-year 5.26%; regulated-utility equity beta ~0.5; ERP 5.0% -> CAPM 7.4%, rounded to 7.5% and held identical across scenarios (risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights). For reference the sector's current ~20x forward P/E on 8-10% growth implies the market is using ~6.5%; the sensitivity grid runs 5.5-9.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for Ameren (no separate lease principal line of consequence); lease cost sits inside O&M, i.e. inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are $129m of subsidiary preferred stock paying ~$5m/yr. Flows are ATTRIBUTABLE to common (pre-tax margin is built net of preferred dividends), so no NCI deduction in the bridge -- charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. dcf-methods SKILL.md has no regulated-utility row; the operating-company row sends a utility to the owner-FCF DCF and the compounder-of-book row to BVPS x exit P/B. The firm-level owner-FCF DCF is unusable here, for the reason documented on AIA.NZ (capex supercycle, DCF NZ$1.90 vs NZ$8.76): Ameren's capex ($4.1bn FY2025, $4.1bn in 9M-2026 alone, up to $46bn 2026-2031) runs ~2x operating cash flow by design, every dollar of it enters rate base and earns an allowed return (MO ~9.5-10%, IL electric 8.72%, IL gas 9.60%, FERC transmission 10.48%), and the interim FCFs are negative for the whole explicit horizon while the terminal year still carries growth capex -- the house 20x-FCF cap then capitalises a depressed number and the model returns negative equity for a company earning an 11% consolidated ROE. The economics of a regulated utility are those of a compounder of book: value = PV of (net income - equity invested in rate-base growth) at the cost of equity, which is exactly the FCFE stream. It is run on the Drivers/engine route in the IAG.AX / GPT.AX / CHC.AX pattern so the dashboard reproduces it: revenue is the driver line; 'ebitda_margin_path' = PRE-TAX INCOME ATTRIBUTABLE TO COMMON as % of revenue (after interest charges and preferred dividends -- it is NOT EBITDA); D&A, SBC and lease paths are 0 (all already inside pre-tax income); cash_tax_rate_path = effective tax rate, so 'NOPAT' = net income attributable; 'capex_pct_path' = the INCREASE IN SHAREHOLDERS' EQUITY required by the rate-base plan (retained earnings PLUS new common stock issued) as % of revenue; FCF line = free cash flow to equity; discount at cost of equity; net debt 0. FY0 equity 13,401 (ex-NCI). Equity issuance is charged at face, so any accretion from issuing at today's ~2.2x book is NOT credited -- conservative. EQUITY NEED PATH: 2026 $0.63bn (6.4m forward shares ~$93 + DRPlus/benefit plans), 2027 $1.3bn, 2028 $1.5bn, 2029 $1.0bn, 2030 $0.7bn, 2031 $0.5bn = $5.0bn 2027-2031, matching the Q3-2026 10-Q ('concentrated primarily near year-end 2027 and year-end 2028'); after 2031 growth is funded from retention only with payout falling from the 45-55% policy range toward ~68% as growth fades. GUIDANCE ANCHORS: FY2026 EPS $5.35-5.55 (base uses $5.55: 9M diluted EPS is already $4.83 and Q4-2025 was $0.92, so even the top of the range implies a soft Q4); FY2027 $5.70-5.90; 8-10% EPS CAGR 2027-2031 (base takes the LOW end 8%, bull 10%, bear ~4%); dividend payout 45-55%; ~13.3% rate-base CAGR. SANITY: base-case FY2026E net income ~$1.55bn on 2026E revenue ~$9.0bn (9M-2026 revenue 7,150, +1.9%). Owner-FCF (firm) CAGRs are undefined because the series is negative in every year since FY2017; historical_growth.fcf_* are null for that reason.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3-yr CAGR (3.4%) is less than half the equity CAGR (8.3%) and EPS CAGR (8.9%). Expected for a regulated utility: revenue carries pass-through fuel/purchased-power and the 2023-24 fuel deflation, while earnings track rate base; equity growth also includes ~$1.2bn of common stock issued 2023-2025, so per-share book compounded at ~5.5%, not 8.3%.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use 10-K diluted EPS: FY2020 $3.50, FY2022 $4.14, FY2025 $5.35. Equity CAGRs use total equity from the Metrics CSV (FY2020 9,080; FY2022 10,637; FY2025 13,530). Firm-level owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC) has been negative every year since FY2017 (FY2025 -803; FY2021 -1,840), so an FCF CAGR is undefined -- recorded as null rather than a spurious figure. This is the capex-supercycle signature, not distress: OCF grew 2,170 (FY2019) -> 3,353 (FY2025), a 7.5% CAGR.

base.growth_rationale: Revenue, FY2025 base 8,799. FY2026 +2.3% (9M-2026 +1.9%; no major base-rate step this year). FY2027 +7% as the Missouri electric case ($343m ask, new rates June 2027) and the IL MYRP 2027 revenue requirement land and the first large-load contracts energise in H2. FY2028-29 +9% as the 2.8 GW of signed data-centre load ramps toward full capacity in 2030 (volume plus fuel pass-through) on top of ~13% rate-base growth. Fades to 3.5% by FY2035 as the capital plan normalises. Revenue grows slower than rate base throughout because the fuel/purchased-power component does not earn a return.
base.margin_rationale: NOT EBITDA: pre-tax income attributable to common / revenue (after interest and preferred dividends). FY2025 actual 18.1% (1,592/8,799); 9M-2026 22.1% but Q4 is seasonally weak (Q4-2025 13.7%). The path is back-solved from the net-income path: FY2026 $5.55 x 278.8m = 1,547; FY2027 $5.80 x ~290m = 1,682; then EPS +8%/yr (LOW end of the 8-10% guidance) on a share count rising to ~332m by 2031 as the $5bn equity plan is issued, giving total NI 2,619 in FY2031 (consolidated ROE ~11%, the FY2025 actual of 11.3% on average equity); FY2032-35 NI +6/5/4/3.5%. Margin rises as the return-on-rate-base component outgrows pass-through revenue; the FY2035 net margin of 19.8% compares with 16.5% in FY2025.
base.capex_rationale: Equity invested in rate-base growth = increase in shareholders' equity (retained earnings + common stock issued) as % of revenue. FY2026: NI 1,547 - dividends 831 ($3.00 x 277m) + issuance 630 = 1,341 (14.9%). FY2027-28 peak at 21-22% as $1.3bn and $1.5bn of equity are raised (management: issuances concentrated near year-end 2027 and 2028) on top of ~45% retention. FY2029-31 fall to 12.5% as issuance tapers ($1.0bn/$0.7bn/$0.5bn; total $5.0bn 2027-31 per the Q3-2026 10-Q). FY2032-35: no issuance; equity grows at the NI growth rate (6/5/4/3.5%) at a constant ~11% ROE, so payout rises from ~45% to 68% by FY2035. Consolidated equity reaches ~$24.5bn by FY2031 against a rate base management guides to ~$60bn (13.3% CAGR from $29.8bn) -- a ~41% consolidated equity ratio, consistent with today's 40% (parent-level debt sits on top of the ~50-52% regulated capital structures).
base.tax_rationale: GAAP effective tax rate (the economically right charge for a regulated utility: cash-tax deferrals reduce rate base through ADIT and are passed to customers). FY2023 13.7%, FY2024 6.5%, FY2025 8.5% (excess-deferred-tax revaluation benefits), 9M-2026 14.6%. Ramps to 19% as excess deferred income tax amortisation winds down, below the ~25% blended statutory rate because of production tax credits on the renewables build. Cash taxes have been a net receipt (-312 FY2025) and do not change equity value.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5% / 3.0% = 22.9x terminal FCFE; with a 68% payout that is ~15.7x FY2036 earnings and ~1.7x book at an 11% ROE -- the textbook steady-state (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) multiple, and a de-rating from today's ~20x forward P/E. The cap is set at 24x FCFE (~16.4x earnings, the long-run US regulated-utility P/E range of 15-17x) so that Gordon binds; a 20x cap would impose a 13.7x exit P/E no regulated utility has traded at outside 2008-09.

bull.growth_rationale: Revenue +8-10% FY2027-30 as the full 2.8 GW of signed large-load demand plus part of the additional 1.2 GW under construction agreements energises on schedule, the Missouri case is settled near the ask, and MISO tranche-2 transmission is added. Fades to 3.5% by FY2035.
bull.margin_rationale: Pre-tax attributable margin back-solved from EPS $5.60 (FY2026), $5.90 (FY2027, top of range) then +10%/yr (TOP of the 2027-31 guidance) on the same rising share count -> total NI 2,868 in FY2031 (ROE ~11.9%, Missouri earning near its 10.25% ask with CWIP in rate base under the PPRA); FY2032-35 NI +7/6/4.5/3.5%.
bull.capex_rationale: Same $5.0bn 2027-31 equity programme and same dividend path as base; the higher earnings are retained, so equity reaches ~$25.2bn by FY2031. No issuance after 2031; payout rises to ~70% by FY2035.

bear.growth_rationale: Revenue +5-6% FY2027-29: the Missouri order lands well below the $343m ask with a sub-10% ROE, the Illinois appeals fail, and only the ~1.2 GW already in guidance materialises on time with the balance slipping past 2030, so part of the capital plan is deferred. Fades to 3% by FY2034.
bear.margin_rationale: Pre-tax attributable margin back-solved from EPS $5.45 (FY2026 midpoint), $5.70 (FY2027 low end), then ~4%/yr -- half the guided range -- as regulatory lag on an enlarged plan, higher-for-longer rates (30-yr UST 5.26%) on $3bn+/yr of new debt, and dilution compress consolidated ROE from 11% to 9.5% by FY2030 (the allowed-ROE level with no parent-leverage uplift). FY2032-35 NI +4/3.5/3/3%.
bear.capex_rationale: Equity still has to be raised for the committed 2026-28 programme ($0.63bn/$1.3bn/$1.4bn) before the plan is trimmed ($0.9bn/$0.6bn/$0.4bn 2029-31; $4.6bn 2027-31 vs $5bn guided) -- the dilution is front-loaded and the earnings growth that was meant to pay for it is not. Dividend growth slowed to ~6%/yr (payout drifts to the top of the 45-55% range). No issuance after 2031; equity grows at 3-4% at a 9.5% ROE, payout ~69% by FY2035.
bear.tax_rationale: Excess deferred tax amortisation rolls off faster and fewer PTC-generating renewables are built, so the effective rate reaches 20%.

scenario_narratives.base: Ameren executes the low end of its own algorithm: FY2026 EPS at the top of the raised $5.35-5.55 range (9M already $4.83), FY2027 $5.80, then 8% compound EPS growth to 2031 on a ~13% rate-base CAGR, with the full ~$5bn of 2027-31 equity issued and charged to today's holders. Consolidated ROE holds at ~11% (allowed ROEs of 8.7-10.5% plus parent-level leverage). After 2031 growth fades to 3.5% and the payout rises toward 68%. The axes that matter are (1) the May-2027 Missouri electric order (10.25% ROE / 52% equity / $16.7bn rate base asked), (2) whether the signed 2.8 GW of data-centre load energises on the H2-2027 to 2030 schedule, and (3) the cost and timing of the equity programme.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-centre pipeline is real and larger than guided: all 2.8 GW plus part of the 1.2 GW under construction agreements energises on time, the PPRA puts new gas generation CWIP into rate base, the Missouri order lands near the ask, MISO tranche-2 transmission is added, and EPS compounds at the top of the 8-10% range through 2031 with the same equity programme -- so the extra earnings are retained and ROE drifts to ~12%. No multiple expansion is assumed: the exit is still ~16x earnings against ~20x today.
scenario_narratives.bear: The growth algorithm is bought with equity before it is earned: $4.6bn of stock is issued 2027-31 while regulatory lag (a sub-10% Missouri ROE, failed Illinois appeals), higher-for-longer financing costs on $3bn+/yr of new debt, and a slower-than-contracted data-centre ramp hold EPS growth to ~4%. Consolidated ROE compresses to 9.5% -- the allowed level with no leverage uplift -- and dividend growth slows to ~6%. This is the 'utility built ahead of its load' outcome the Analysis JSON flags as its highest-severity risk.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 30%: the Analysis JSON rates data-centre materialisation risk, the pending Missouri rate case and interest-rate sensitivity all 'high'; only ~1.2 GW of the 2.8 GW is in guidance so the plan is sized ahead of contracted revenue; the equity programme is front-loaded into 2027-28 regardless of outcome; and the 30-year Treasury at 5.26% is the highest financing backdrop of the capital plan's life. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs four independent things to go right at once (full load ramp, a constructive Missouri order, Illinois appeals, MISO tranche-2) and the base case already assumes management delivers the bottom of an industry-leading growth range. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a compounder of book: it earns an allowed return on equity invested in rate base and grows by putting more equity in. The value to today's shareholders is the present value, at the cost of equity, of net income less the equity the plan requires (retained AND newly issued). That stream is negative in FY2027-28 while the $5bn equity programme is raised, turns positive as rate-base growth outpaces equity needs, and is capitalised at a steady-state (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) multiple of ~1.7x book / ~16x earnings. Firm-level FCF is deliberately not the valuation flow -- it is negative by design in a capex supercycle and a Gordon/cap terminal on it values a healthy 11%-ROE utility at less than nothing (AIA.NZ precedent). The house 15% hurdle entry price is reported but is close to unreachable for a 7.5%-cost-of-equity asset: it requires buying at roughly half of intrinsic value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 7.5% discount rate moves the base value ~12-14%; the market's ~20x forward P/E implies ~6.5%, this model's 7.5% tracks a 4.86% 10-year Treasury
Missouri electric rate order due May 2027 ($343m ask, 10.25% ROE, 52% equity, $16.7bn rate base) -- the single largest regulatory input to FY2027-28 earnings
Data-centre load: 2.8 GW signed but only ~1.2 GW in guidance; capex is being committed ahead of energisation (H2-2027 to 2030)
Equity financing: ~$5bn 2027-31 charged at face; issuance at today's ~2.2x book would be accretive to this value, issuance in a de-rated market would not cover it
Illinois: 8.72% MYRP ROE and reconciliation cap under appeal; 2025 gas order appealed; Grid Plan 2028-31 order due Dec 2026
Tax: excess-deferred-tax amortisation and PTC transferability under the OBBBA/IRA; the effective rate ramps 13.5% -> 19% and each point is ~1.2% of net income
Coal retirements by 2042 and up to 1,200 MW of new nuclear in the 2026 PRP -- long-dated execution and prudence-review risk
